description:
Search open jobs on Ocean of Jobs. Give at least one of query, company, city or country (IL for Israel; most listings are in the US). Returns up to 25 jobs per call, best match first when there is a query, newest first otherwise, with the total number of matches. Every job includes its lifetime (days listed, first and last seen) and two links: url, the Ocean of Jobs page, to show first, and apply_url, the employer's page.

How to search well:
- Put one or two core title or skill words in query, such as "backend", "python" or "devops", and use the filters for place, seniority and dates. Every word in query must match, so a long description of the person returns little or nothing.
- Search once. If that gives relevant candidates, do not search again for synonyms. If it gives nothing useful, change or broaden query once, keeping the same filters.
- Across searches, treat the same id or the same apply_url as one job.
- Open only the strongest few candidates with get_job, and read their descriptions for seniority, required skills and where the job can be done from before ranking them.
- Give the number of recommendations asked for when enough jobs fit, and say so when fewer do.
- Never call a listing reposted because of its age. Use lifetime.reappeared_at, and say when the tracked history is too short to tell.

company.description: A company domain such as wix.com, or a name, which is looked up.

country.description: Two-letter country code, e.g. IL or US.

max_age_days.description: Only jobs posted within this many days.

query.description: Words to search titles, companies, locations and descriptions, skills included, e.g. "kubernetes go". Quotes keep a phrase together.

salary_min.description: Lowest monthly gross salary in shekels.

name: search_jobs

duplicates_folded.description: Rows on this page that were the same posting as another, folded into it.

company.description: The employer's name, or its domain when the ATS gives no name.

lifetime.description: first_seen is when Ocean of Jobs first found the listing on the employer's own applicant tracking system. last_seen is the last time a read of that board returned the listing with any change; a board that answers 'unchanged' was still checked, so the listing may have been confirmed more recently than last_seen says. closed_at is when a successful read of the board no longer included it; null means it was still listed at the last successful read. reappeared_at is when this same listing (the same ATS id) was last seen again after being missing from our reads of the board for at least two days; null means no such absence was seen (recorded since 2026-10-19). It says what was observed, not that the employer reposted it: our own failed reads can look the same, so do not call a listing reposted on this or on an old first_seen. A new posting for the same role is a new listing. posted_at is the employer's own date where the ATS gives one, and can be missing.

other_locations.description: Other places the same posting is listed for.

salary.description: Monthly, in shekels, as listed or estimated.

url.description: The listing's page on Ocean of Jobs. Show this first.

total.description: Every match, not only this page.

title: Search jobs
